newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen higher, continuing rally.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen higher, continuing rally.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to head higher at the open, following through on a powerful, broad-based rally that took the Dow Industrials to their first close above 6900 on Wednesday.
The wild card could be January retail sales, due at 0830 EST/1330 GMT. A too-strong figure could undermine the bond market and weaken equities, analysts said.
Hildegard Zagorski, analyst at Prudential Securities, said the Dow Industrials had a good chance to reach 7,000 by week's end.

"I think we will probably have a decent opening. There might be some profit-taking at the start, but the market is back in gear on the upside," Zagorski said. "Whatever happens in the morning, by the time we close we'll be back on the upside."
Stronger-than-expected retail sales would be only a temporary hurdle for the market, she said.

"The retail sales are important, but I think 7,000 on the Dow is a sure thing," she said. "It is not outside the realm of possibility that it will happen today. It is certainly likely that we will get there by the end of trading Friday."
In Tokyo the Nikkei Average finished up 278.10 points, or 1.51 percent, at 18,688.06.
In London the FTSE 100 Index was up 16.7 points at 4321.
U.S. stocks in London were mixed. Dealers said high techs were marginally firmer, auto stocks were mixed, and some drug stocks fell prey to profit-taking.
The dollar eased against the mark and yen in Tokyo and was aimless in Europe.
U.S. Treasuries were flat to lower, with the long bond down 1/32 to yield 6.71 percent.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column said that with pilots of American Airlines threatening to strike, the risks for investors in parent AMR Corp could hardly be more stark. A quick settlement with the pilots could boost the stock, but a long walkout could trigger a steady fall, it said.

The New York Times's Market Place column said analysts have been raising new questions about how costly America Online Inc's business strategy is proving to be, whether it has the cash to execute its plans, and how long it will take the company to show steady profits.
